caution: Operator shorthand for a generalised flux law. No source prints this notation with a script D; it is review-internal. It is harmless as shorthand but cannot be cited, and its content is entirely in whichever closure is substituted into it.

caution: Ezzat and El Karamany print the first-order expansion of the lagged flux, flux plus relaxation time times flux rate equals minus conductivity times temperature gradient. The manuscript display is identical after renaming theta to T. Give the display a number so it can be anchored.

caution: Follows by Laplace transform of the printed Cattaneo law (12) with zero initial flux. caution: Same equation as eq:4.20 and eq:11.1, so the same cautions apply: the source's order symbol is beta while the display uses alpha, which also denotes the thermal displacement in Sections 4 and 11. Repeat the symbol map wherever this display recurs, or a reader will read the fractional order as the thermal displacement.
assumptions_stated: Caputo derivative, constant diffusivity, heat-conduction postulate.

caution: The source's time-nonlocal law is q(t) = -k * integral from -infinity to t of K(t-tau) grad T(tau) dtau, i.e. exactly the generic memory functional of the display with an unbounded past. The source then re-derives the same law with a finite lower limit (its next equation) and states plainly that changing the starting point changes the model - so the display's lower limit is a modelling choice, not a convention.
assumptions_stated: Linear time-nonlocal constitutive law; kernel to be chosen; the starting point of memory is part of the model.

caution: Wang and Li define the first-order memory-dependent derivative as one over the delay times the integral over the slipping interval of kernel times the ordinary derivative; the manuscript matches with omega_M for the delay and K_MDD for the kernel. Their eq (7) on p.1564 gives the unit-kernel limit used in the manuscript text, and confirms that doubling the kernel doubles the limit while dropping the one-over-delay prefactor sends the limit to zero. Symbol caution: the source calls the delay tau, which the manuscript already uses for the relaxation time, so omega_M is the correct choice.
assumptions_stated: Kernel differentiable in its arguments, delay positive, function differentiable on the interval; the source leaves the kernel choice free.

caution: Convention definition, not a sourced equation. It is the exponential special case of the arbitrary-profile plane wave that Yang writes on p.113 (4.2). Two points the text already makes should stay: the sign of the imaginary part of the wavenumber reverses if the opposite time convention is adopted, and complex amplitudes conjugate. No script covers this display; it is a definition.
assumptions_stated: Linear time-invariant problem, real frequency, complex amplitude field.

caution: Printed as (Gamma_jk - rho v^2 delta_jk) A_k = 0 with Gamma_jk = c_ijkl n_l n_i + (piezoelectric term) and Gamma symmetric. Same eigenvalue problem as the display, with c = phase speed in place of v. Two cautions: (i) in the source Gamma is the PIEZOELEVTRICALLY STIFFENED tensor - for a purely elastic medium the second term is absent, so the display must say which medium it describes; (ii) the manuscript uses c both for phase speed here and for elastic stiffness elsewhere, and the source deliberately uses v for speed for exactly that reason.
assumptions_stated: Homogeneous plane wave in an unbounded region; real symmetric acoustic tensor; infinitesimal linear piezoelectricity.

caution: The determinantal condition is printed verbatim in form. The source adds what the display leaves implicit: the determinant is a cubic in v^2, all three roots are real because the acoustic tensor is real symmetric, and the three eigenvectors are orthogonal. Dropping that sentence makes the display look like a generic solvability condition rather than a three-branch dispersion result.
assumptions_stated: Real symmetric acoustic tensor; three real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors follow.

caution: Manuscript template. No held source prints a generic even-power secular polynomial with symbolic coefficients; the closest printed statement is Yang p.114 (4.9), which is a cubic in the squared speed for the bulk elastic case. Because the display fixes no order and no coefficients it asserts little, but the surrounding sentence must keep saying that the order is model-dependent.
assumptions_stated: The secular equation of the selected model must be polynomial and even in the spectral variable; admissibility of roots is set by boundary and radiation conditions.

caution: Normalisation convention chosen by the manuscript for flux bookkeeping over unit polarization. It is a definition, and the text already warns that evanescent modes need a stated convention and that cross terms are not fixed by modal amplitudes. No script covers it.
assumptions_stated: Propagating modes only, nonzero amplitude, complex conjugate convention as in eq:3.27.

caution: Fourier transform definition with the positive exponent, which is the consistent partner of the time convention in eq:8.1. It is a definition, so there is nothing to check against a source; what does need care is that the pair must stay consistent if either sign is changed.
assumptions_stated: Bilateral transform exists; integrability or distributional interpretation stated where used.

caution: One-sided Laplace transform definition. Definition only; the text correctly ties its use to transformability and to initial-data bookkeeping, which is where the memory and fractional sections diverge from the classical case.
assumptions_stated: Causal signal, transform converges on a right half-plane; initial values handled per application.

caution: Harmonic plane wave with depth dependence, written for a boundary-value problem in x3. It is the assembled form of the convention in eq:8.1 plus the in-plane phase; no held source prints this exact combination. Consistent with Yang p.113 (4.2).
assumptions_stated: Homogeneous layer, propagation along x1, depth dependence retained, time-harmonic.

caution: Partial-wave superposition in each half-space. Manuscript assembly; Yang does not print a summed partial-wave ansatz. The admissible q roots and the count per medium are what the mode-count script checks; the sum itself is a definition.
assumptions_stated: Finite number of retained roots per medium; radiation or decay conditions applied to each root separately.

caution: Yang prints the mechanical jump conditions of a welded interface as continuity of displacement and of the traction vector. The manuscript restricts to the x3 tractions, which is correct only for the flat interface at x3 = 0 with no in-plane variation of the interface; state that restriction.
assumptions_stated: Welded contact, flat interface, no interfacial mass or stiffness.

caution: Thermal jump conditions. Not printed in the held Yang chapters as a thermal pair; the closest printed statements are for the mechanical and electrical pairs. The condition as written holds only when there is no interfacial heat source and no interfacial thermal resistance; both must be stated.
assumptions_stated: No interfacial heat source, no contact resistance, temperature continuous.

caution: Yang prints potential continuity plus the normal-displacement jump equal to the free surface charge, and the zero-charge case used here. Keep the free-charge condition explicit, otherwise the continuity of D3 is not the general statement.
assumptions_stated: No free charge at the interface, or an unelectroded interface; potential continuous.

caution: Spring-type imperfect bonding. No held source prints this form; it is a model choice, and the stiffness tensor must be declared positive semi-definite and dimensionally consistent (traction per unit displacement). Covered structurally by verify_interface_mode_counts.py, which builds the boundary system and counts modes; that script does not validate the physics of the spring law.
assumptions_stated: Linear springs, traction continuity across the interface, no interfacial inertia.

caution: Notation for the assembled boundary system. Definitional; the only real content is the ordering of the unknown vector, which must match eq:9.8 and the determinant condition.
assumptions_stated: Number of unknowns equals number of boundary equations, as built by verify_interface_mode_counts.py.

caution: Formal inversion of eq:9.7. Valid only while the boundary matrix is nonsingular; a singular matrix is precisely the secular case of eq:9.9, so the two must not be used in the same sentence without a qualifier.
assumptions_stated: Boundary matrix nonsingular; square system.

caution: Existence condition for a nontrivial mode. It is the multi-medium analogue of Yang p.114 (4.9); the source prints only the bulk single-medium determinant. Caution to keep: it is a condition on the retained root set, so it is only meaningful after the admissibility filters of eq:9.2 are applied.
assumptions_stated: Determinant condition, retained-root set fixed, no repeated roots assumed.

caution: Manuscript derivation from the flux definitions in eq:9.10. Verified for the lossless one-dimensional welded case by verify_interface_energy.py, including the negative check that the sum departs from one when an interfacial sink is added, in which case eq:9.12 is the correct statement. State the lossless assumption next to the display.
assumptions_stated: Lossless interface, real impedances, no interfacial storage, propagating modes only.

caution: Definition of the total energy density as kinetic plus internal. Standard; no held source page prints it, and none is needed. It must be used with the small-amplitude convention declared in the section, otherwise the convective part of the flux in eq:10.2 is not complete.
assumptions_stated: Small amplitude, single constituent, no electromagnetic energy included.

caution: Time-averaged flux obtained by applying the product rule of eq:3.27 to the reduced flux of eq:10.3. Derivation, not a quotation; the one-dimensional version is exercised by verify_interface_energy.py. Caution: the real part of a product of two complex amplitudes is not the product of the real parts, which is the mistake the display exists to prevent.
assumptions_stated: Harmonic steady state, averaging over a period, no cross terms between different frequencies.

caution: Interfacial power balance. Manuscript derivation; not printed in the held sources. Its content is that the normal flux jump is the interfacial power input minus the rate of change of interfacial stored energy, which is only meaningful once the interfacial model is declared.
assumptions_stated: Interface treated as a surface of zero thickness with its own power input and stored energy.

caution: Lossless steady interface case of eq:10.5. Verified by verify_interface_energy.py for the welded lossless case; the script also shows the case where it fails, so the assumption must sit next to the display.
assumptions_stated: No interfacial power input, no interfacial storage, steady state.

caution: Reduction of the full interfacial balance eq:10.11 with all absorption and storage terms set to zero. Verified by verify_interface_energy.py in one dimension; the general multi-mode case would need the cross-term convention of eq:8.5 stated.
assumptions_stated: Lossless, steady, no interfacial storage, no bulk absorption in the retained modes.

caution: The printed energy equation in terms of the heat flux, credited there to Biot, is the linearised isotropic case of the manuscript display: the time derivative of heat capacity times temperature change plus coupling times dilatation equals minus the flux divergence plus the source. The manuscript writes the general internal-energy-rate form, so the reduction assumptions (linear, isotropic, small strain, no couple stresses) must be stated; with a source it is the same equation after the stated identifications.
assumptions_stated: Linear isotropic thermoelasticity, no dissipation other than conduction, single heat source.

caution: Source-free case of eq:3.13, obtained by setting the heat supply to zero in the printed equation. Same assumptions as eq:3.13; the display must be tied to the source-free window, since the source term is order one in the applications of Sections 4 and 6.
assumptions_stated: As eq:3.13, with zero heat supply.

caution: Rearrangement of the printed reduced energy equation: stress power minus the rate of free energy and of entropy times temperature minus the flux-gradient term equals minus density times temperature times the internal entropy production. So the display is correct provided the source term is identified with minus the production, and provided the entropy flux is written as heat flux over temperature. Sign convention is the point of failure; verify it symbol by symbol.
assumptions_stated: Entropy flux equal to heat flux divided by temperature; internal production retained; material description in the source.

caution: The chain-rule split of the free-energy rate is the first step of the printed identity the source uses to extract constitutive restrictions. It is valid only if the free energy is a function of strain and temperature alone; for the generalized families of Sections 6, 7 and 11 it carries extra arguments, and the display would then be wrong. Say which class of models the split is written for.
assumptions_stated: Free energy depends on strain and temperature only; no internal variables; small strain.

caution: The state laws are what survives when the reduced energy identity is required to hold for arbitrary rates. The source uses the entropy with a minus sign of the free-energy temperature derivative, as the manuscript does. Caution: the source works with the Piola stress and a reference density, so the density factor sits differently at finite strain; in the small-strain form the placement is immaterial but say so.
assumptions_stated: Arbitrary strain and temperature rates; small-strain reduction; no internal variables.

caution: The printed dissipation reduction requires the conductivity tensor contracted with the temperature gradient to be non-negative in this sense, which is the same as the manuscript inequality once Fourier conduction is substituted. It is not a statement that the conductivity is isotropic; the tensor form must be kept if anisotropy is used in Sections 5 and 9.
assumptions_stated: Fourier conduction, positive definite conductivity, temperature positive.

caution: The printed quadratic free energy for the linear thermopiezoelectric case contains the elastic term, the thermoelastic coupling term with a minus sign, and a temperature-squared term tied to the specific heat; the manuscript display is the elastic plus coupling part with the piezoelectric terms dropped. Two cautions: the source states the approximation on the temperature ratio explicitly, and the manuscript adds a linear-in-temperature gauge term that the source does not carry, which must be declared as a gauge choice.
assumptions_stated: Reference temperature close to the current temperature, quadratic truncation, small strain and small field.

caution: The printed mechanical jump conditions for a welded interface are continuity of displacement and of the traction vector; the manuscript adds temperature and normal heat flux continuity, which the source does not print as a pair. Keep the thermal half separately anchored (see eq:9.4) and state that there is no interfacial heat source or resistance.
assumptions_stated: Welded contact, no interfacial mass, stiffness or heat source; flat interface.

caution: Spring-type imperfect bonding is a model choice in this review; no held source prints it. It is built and its mode counts are checked by verify_interface_mode_counts.py, which also records the square-system requirement. The stiffness tensor must be declared symmetric, positive semi-definite and of dimension traction per displacement; none of that is in a source we hold.
assumptions_stated: Linear interface springs, traction continuity, square boundary system, no interfacial inertia.

caution: The printed statement is that the potential is continuous across an interface, with the general jump of the normal electric displacement carrying the free surface charge; the manuscript display is the perfect-contact case. Word the display so it cannot be read as covering an interface electrode.
assumptions_stated: Perfect electrical contact, no interfacial charge layer, quasi-electrostatic limit.

caution: Printed normal-displacement jump equals free surface charge; the manuscript states continuity, which is the zero-charge case. Same caution as eq:5.12 and eq:5.13, and the same restriction to a flat interface.
assumptions_stated: No free charge at the interface, flat interface, no in-plane variation.

caution: Yang prints the joint conditions for a piezoelectric bimaterial as continuity of displacement, of the relevant traction components, of the potential and of the normal electric displacement; the manuscript display is that last member alone, written as a free-surface condition. Restate as the surface condition it is, or keep it with the interface pair.
assumptions_stated: Traction-free or unelectroded surface, no free charge, flat boundary.

caution: Follows from the Riemann-Liouville integral of the Caputo equation, both printed in the appendix. For orders below one the single initial value T(0) is enough; for orders up to two, as eq:11.1 allows, an extra initial-rate term appears and the display as written is incomplete. State the order range with the display.
assumptions_stated: Zero to one order, single initial value, integrable derivative; spatial operator homogeneous.

caution: The strain-gradient law is the zero stress-gradient case of the printed gradient elasticity equation, with the gradient coefficient equal to the square of the internal length. Symbol caution: Aifantis writes c1 and c2 without fixing their dimensions beyond length squared, and treats them as phenomenological, not derived.
assumptions_stated: Isotropic linear elasticity, small strain, positive internal length squared.

caution: NOT-CHECKED as sourced: the held Mindlin paper is the second-gradient theory, which balances a double stress and prints the symmetry of the ordinary stress, not the antisymmetric-part plus couple-stress-divergence relation displayed. The couple-stress and micropolar balances are standard (Mindlin and Tiersten 1962; Eringen micropolar) but no copy is held, so this display is marked unavailable rather than wrong, and no citation should be forced until a copy is read.
assumptions_stated: Cosserat-type medium with couple stresses, non-polar or polar variant must be stated; small deformation.

caution: A printed source does exist, which was not established before: Ezzat and El Karamany p.940 (15), crediting Youssef, writes the difference of the conductive and thermodynamic temperatures equal to a coefficient times the Laplacian OF THE CONDUCTIVE TEMPERATURE, with a plus sign. The manuscript puts the Laplacian on the thermodynamic temperature with a minus sign. The two agree only to first order in the coefficient; as printed they are different equations. Restate in the source form and define which temperature is which.
assumptions_stated: Two-temperature theory, small difference between the two temperatures, coefficient of dimension length squared.

caution: Modelling definition introduced by this review: a five-component index vector over the axis resolutions. No source prints it and none should be cited. The text already says the first two coordinates gate comparability, which is the assumption that carries the weight.
assumptions_stated: Each coordinate is an index into the stated axis resolution; a study receives one vector.

caution: Modelling definition of an axis-weighted dissimilarity, with the weight ordering declared in the text as a decision of the review. Checked: no script computes this metric. The nearest gate, verify_q3_status_matrix.py, only checks that the fourteen-family status matrix is complete and linked to ledger rows, so it does not support the metric. Note for the writer: Section 14 speaks of a twelve-family grouping while that scripted matrix has fourteen families, and the two counts are never reconciled in the text.
assumptions_stated: Weights fixed by the review, delta is the Kronecker delta, coordinates are categorical indices.
